title: Noisy influence upper bound
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $i\in[n]$, and $0\le\rho\le1$. Then $I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
replaced:
For $0 \le \rho \le 1$ we have
$\mathrm{Inf}_i^{\rho}[f] \le \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ for every coordinate $i$.
